content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies how to find subsets of auxiliary datasets that are most aligned with a target dataset. To this end, this paper proposes to conduct dataset projection and explores a new framework for solving the project problem. Empirical results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Ups: 
+ Finding the target-aligned auxiliary subsets is an important task. This helps to decrease sources of unwanted biases, amplify useful features, and ultimately improve task performance
+ The idea of decoupling the auxiliary data distribution into several source distributions and then finding a combination for them to fit the target distribution is reasonable.
+ Empirical results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.


Downs:
- In Figure 1, what's the original performance of CIFAR10? It is better to provide such a baseline in Figure 1, so that we can better understand the benefit of additional data.
- In Figure 2, even with a target-aligned strategy, the model performance is still first improved and then decreased to the "Train only" baseline. Does this mean that some of the selected target-aligned data are also harmful?
- In Figure 3, this paper provides a synthetic example to explain that using all auxiliary data may lead to inconsistent model distribution to the target data and thus poor performance. However, this may also lead to a waste of precious auxiliary data. It is better to provide a baseline that trains the model with all ImageNet and CIFAR-10 for the same epochs, but the first 80% of epochs are using both datasets while the last 20% of epochs are using only CIFAR10. This baseline is like the manner of fine-tuning models after full mixup training [A]. This scheme helps to tune the model distribution to the target one and also takes full advantage of auxiliary data. It is interesting to know whether down-sampling is a better solution than adaptive training. The results in Appendix D.1 also show that projection sub-sampling may not be a better solution, since inaccurate projection may discard precious and useful samples, leading to worse performance.  
[A] Bag of Tricks for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks. In AAAI, 2021.
- It is well-known that many samples in the auxiliary set are unrelated or less related to the target dataset. This leads Section 2 to be less valuable, since the main take-away message of Section 2 is this well-known knowledge. Instead, it is better for authors to conduct experiments to observe how the auxiliary data help model training where the target dataset also exists, and observe whether sampling suitable auxiliary data can lead to significant performance improvement than using all auxiliary data. 
- In Eq. (3), please clarify why to choose a linear combination. Any intuition on it? 
- In Section 3, the authors argue that "our framework can project any auxiliary dataset on onto any target dataset, including those with different labels or no labels at all". This argument is too strong in my view. Can the proposed method work for augmenting medical image samples with auxiliary natural image samples？ How much accuracy gain does the resulting model gain from such a projection? 
- In Section 4.1, does closeness means effectiveness and usefulness? Please discuss this and verify it. It seems that Appendix D.1 provides a counter-example. 
- Figure 7 provides some visualization, which is good. It is better to also provide some failure cases and discussions.
- The explored setting is similar to semi-supervised learning to some degree. Please discuss this paradigm in related work. It is also better to compare some classic semi-supervised methods as baselines. 
- In Table 8, why does target-only performance is different for the same target dataset?
- Minor issue: there is a redundant "in" at the end of the fourth contribution on Page 2.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarify is overall okay. Quality needs to be improved. Novelty can be improved.  Reproducibility is good thanks to the provided source code.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall, I agree that finding the target-aligned auxiliary subsets is an important task, whose ultimate goal is to improve task performance. However, there are a series of issues that need to be resolved, which limits the quality of this paper. 

*************
Post rebuttal: the authors did not provide any response, so I keep the original judgment. Considering that finding the target-aligned auxiliary subsets is interesting, I expect that the authors can further improve this work based on the provided suggestions.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This work focuses on data selection for improving the final performance of the target dataset. The authors conducted an experiment to demonstrate that directly combing the auxiliary dataset and target dataset would make the performance on the target dataset drop. This is because not all samples or subsets of the auxiliary dataset share the same or similar distribution with the target dataset.
To handle this issue, the authors proposed utilizing MMD to calculate the distance between subsets in the auxiliary dataset and target dataset. And then, active set, and quadratic program are used to locate the most related subsets in the auxiliary dataset. Those selected subsets are utilized for training as they are expected to benefit the final performance of the target dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

-- The motivation for this work is solid and correct. The authors provided experimental proof to explain the necessity of the solution.

-- The organization of the writing is good and easy to follow. The experimental results are extensive.

Weakness:
What concerns me the most is the technical contribution and novelty of this work.
-- This work is actually based on data selection. The authors directly utilize some existing selection methods, such as active set, and quadratic program to select the subsets, rather than making their own contributions on this part. 

-- The distance metric between subsets is MMD, which is also utilized many times in prior works.

-- It seems that the authors assume that samples in the same class are in IID. Does this really hold in practical cases? It is very often in real scenarios that samples in the same classes are from different distributions.
"For the remainder of this paper, we will assume the target distribution q to be a class-wise subset of the target dataset"

-- Utilising external dataset as an auxiliary dataset is related to omni-supervised learning. It would be better to point this out and list some references in the related work.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This submission is written in good clarity and fair quality. Its technical contribution, in my point of view, is not strong enough.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Generally, this work targets the dataset section and omni-supervised learning. The writing is clear enough and easy to follow. The authors conducted extensive experiments to explain the motivation and demonstrate the efficacy of their solution.
What concerns me is the technical contribution of this work. MMD, active set, and quadratic programming, neither of them is new and has been utilized in prior works. I can not find any modifications conducted by the authors.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies the problem of dataset project, which aims at finding the subsets of an auxiliary datasets for additional training datasets, to improve performance on the target datasets. To achieve this, this paper introduces to an automated algorithm that selects data from the source distribution that are well-aligned with target distribution. Particularly, this paper argue that such found sub datasets can often improve the generalization performance on the target datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

+ This paper has shown that indiscriminate use of auxiliary dataset can hurt model's performance on certain target tasks & datasets, via both empirical observation on real-world datasets and controlled experiments on synthetic datasets.

+ This paper also introduces to use this motivation and develop algorithm that actively samples subsets of training data, such that it can improve the performance on downstream tasks. 

Weakness:

- The motivation of dataset projection is not clear to me. It sounds like the existence of some unwanted biases in pre-training datasets are hurting model's performance but I can't see why selecting data using automated approach can ensure such biases are removed. The MMD based objective to me is just to make the pre-training datasets more aligned with the target datasets. 

- Meanwhile, this paper assumes that models are trained using the auxiliary data together with the target data, which is not the most popular recipe in current models. Instead, most of the models are trained via first pre-training on the a large datasets (to learn robust and generalization featurization), and then fine-tuned on the target dataset (to leverage task-specific inductive bias, and remove biases from pre-training data). This assumption make the applicability of the proposed problem very narrow. 

- For many experiments that is shown in this paper, I have a hard time to believe the conclusion particularly as they goes against some basic reasoning based on well-known facts from the literature. 

Questions: 

= I am not exactly sure if I follow the experiments on Figure 1. Suppose we all agree that pre-trained classifiers on ImageNet can improve the model's performance CIFAR 100, and that this paper is suggesting adding data from only relevant ImageNet classes are hurting the performance, then does it mean that training signals from the some irrelevant ImageNet classes are beneficial to the transfer performance on CIFAR 100? 

If the reasoning behind adding more ImageNet is biasing the distribution of CIFAR 100 datasets so the performance is degenerating, why can not people choose to perform a two stage approach: 1. pre-train on ImageNet relevant classes. 2. fine-tune on CIFAR100 in-domain data? This sounds to me a more reasonable setting comparing to the dataset projection

= In the introduction, this paper has claimed that "In particular, intelligently and automatically selected subsets of auxiliary data have the potential to decrease sources of unwanted biases, amplify useful features, and ultimately improve task performance", is there any evidence that supports the claim? From my perspective, I would argue the opposite statement, that such selected data that in fact increase the risk of posing biases from the data selector into the data, and further amplify the unwanted biases in eventual model.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
I think the overall writing is clear. 

The quality of experiments are not good enough. 

The technical novelty is rather limited as I see it similar to domain adaptation methods such as "Reshaping Visual Datasets for Domain Adaptation". As the authors have claimed, the key difference is the setting, where they assume target datasets with label and the auxiliary dataset without. 

I believe reproducibility is good.
content.summary_of_the_review: Based on my comments on strength and weakness, I would not recommend this paper for acceptance. I think more work needs to be done to convince people why the assumed training setting must be used.
